verdict.rationale: Quo documents an explicit date-based versioning scheme: a required Quo-Api-Version header with no default, versions frozen on ship, and an enumerated list of breaking changes. Its deprecation policy commits to changelog announcements with a migration window, and the legacy v1 API stays supported under that notice; dated OpenAPI documents for both versions corroborate the scheme. Missing for 10: a stated minimum length for the migration window, independent or hands-on corroboration of the policy in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Every version is a date. Every request declares which date it was built for
A version is frozen the day it ships.
No version disappears quietly. If a version is ever scheduled for retirement, we'll announce it in the changelog with a migration window and a precise list of what changed.
